treatments.name: Individualized HbA1c targets
treatments.population: Nonpregnant outpatient adults with type 2 diabetes
treatments.summary: Glycemic goals should be personalised; for most patients the target HbA1c is 7% to 8%.

evidence.quote: Clinicians should personalize goals for glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes on the basis of a discussion of benefits and harms of pharmacotherapy, patients' preferences, patients' general health and life expectancy, treatment burden, and costs of care.
evidence.statement: Glycemic goals should be personalised through discussion of benefits, harms, preferences, health, life expectancy, burden and cost.

evidence.quote: Clinicians should aim to achieve an HbA1c level between 7% and 8% in most patients with type 2 diabetes.
evidence.statement: ACP sets an HbA1c target of 7% to 8% for most patients.

treatments.name: Deintensification of pharmacologic therapy
treatments.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes with HbA1c below 6.5% or limited life expectancy
treatments.summary: Consider deintensifying when HbA1c is below 6.5%, and avoid targeting HbA1c when life expectancy is under 10 years.

evidence.quote: Clinicians should consider deintensifying pharmacologic therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes who achieve HbA1c levels less than 6.5%.
evidence.statement: Drug therapy should be reduced when HbA1c falls below 6.5%.

evidence.quote: avoid targeting an HbA1c level in patients with a life expectancy less than 10 years due to advanced age (80 years or older), residence in a nursing home, or chronic conditions
evidence.statement: For people with limited life expectancy, treat symptoms rather than an HbA1c target.

notes: Guidance statement reviewing other national guidelines on HbA1c targets.
